title: I created a 24/7 stream where GPT, Claude, and Gemini play a board game against each other
author: DntWry0

comments.author: Kalaminator
comments.body:
Self promotion and no links? 

More than this it would be cool to make them create a JS trainer for bots and see who builds the stronger bot. Then try the same with a python Jax engine. I might be wrong, but I will guess AI on their own are not very good players.

replies.author: DntWry0
replies.body: Reddit filters were having a field day with my post so I tried just posting without a link. That would also be a great concept to implement as well. Yes, you make a valid point they may not be good players but we can see which one is the best option.

comments.author: voyager2005
comments.body: this looks like Catan almost lol

replies.author: DntWry0
replies.body: Yea, its built on Catanatron, an open-source engine for that style of game. Since I'm not affiliated with any board game company, I keep all the naming and art original.

comments.author: Pix4Geeks
comments.body:
I love the idea. 

Can you explain a bit how the LLM interacts with the game ? I have in mind to create an agent that plays the game I'm vibe-coding, but I have no idea how it should work (I haven't made research either though)

replies.author: DntWry0
replies.body: I looked up some options for this and found that there was actually an open source engine Catanatron that existed that I was able to utilize. I just needed to build my ui on top and provide it the model. The important part I learned was making sure the model only saw what it needs to see like its own resources and cards and the public board rather than cheating and seeing the spectators view of all the models resources. In your case, it’d be easier if you could expose all the legal moves you want the models to perform and have them select a valid option to progress with. Also make sure to log token usage to make sure you see which model is worth utilizing.
